g.text: A manager reviews six fictional accounts and chooses two interventions. Local work stays in the browser. Shared work goes through the API.
+ Familiar flow for reviewing a full portfolio
+ Evidence and saved plan share one detail panel
Choose Ember + Cove: deadline and actionable issue.
API confirms the save after commit

Request corrected report; retain unknown values
Confirm approver and decision date this week
Monitor until new evidence or renewal review
Cove has conflicting signals; Drift has a data gap.
Request a corrected usage report for Drift.
Zero slots used. Adoption stays Unknown.
Try to save a Cove plan without an owner.
The editor asks for an owner and keeps the draft.
Give Cove an owner and a follow-up two days from today.
One slot used. The saved evidence, owner and date survive reload.
Resolve Cove’s critical issue under Owner actions.
Cove moves to Follow-up planned. Its plan still occupies a slot.
Save an Ember plan, then try adding a Beacon plan.
Ember fills the second slot. Beacon waits until a plan is completed.
Static Next.js dashboard on Vercel. The local portfolio uses
One profile keeps its local plans across reloads and tabs.
Environment selection determines which board receives a save.
pnpm dev starts the frontend and API through Turbo.
Use the Firestore emulator for isolated shared writes and resets.
The local portfolio works with the API offline.
Go on Cloud Run in Iowa. Commands and reset use POST.
GET /workbench/accounts lists a page for API clients.
The API checks revisions and capacity before committing changes.
OpenAPI and Scalar describe the request and error contracts.
The browser subscribes to workbenches/shared. A committed
change reaches every browser watching the demo board.
Firestore rules allow get on the shared document. Only the API
identity can write. Browser writes and collection listing are denied.
A background health check enables Shared API. If it goes down,
the local board is available and editors keep their destination.
On recovery the saved Shared API preference takes effect once
open dialogs close. Local saves stay in IndexedDB.
Unit prices · US dollars · November 2026 planning model
Model request-based billing in us-central1 with no idle instances.
1 vCPU, 512 MiB and 0.2 billed seconds per request.
Default database in us-central1. Free quotas include 1 GiB
50k reads and 20k writes free daily. Overage per 100k:
Public static demo: 0.5 MB of assets per reviewer per month.
Hosting: $0 for an eligible public demo. Soft bandwidth limit:
100 GB/month. Commercial SaaS needs another host.
Five CDN requests per reviewer per month. At 100,000 reviewers:
500,000 requests and 50 GB of static assets.
Eligible personal Hobby demo: $0 within quotas.
Pro: from $20/month for one seat, plus applicable overages.
Occasional builds, small retained image and modest logs.
Assume available free quotas; these do not scale per user.
$0 assumed here. Excludes excess builds, images, logs,
API network egress, taxes, support and custom domains.
Monthly cost scenario · core services (USD) · up to 100,000 monthly reviewers
Attention rules · fixed thresholds · explainable checks, not predictions
Scenario per reviewer per month: 100 API calls, 300 document reads, 150 writes, eight deletes and 2 MiB of Firestore outbound traffic.
Reads include snapshots, reconnects and transactions. Deletes budget for cleanup in a larger portfolio. The demo reset rewrites one document.
Spread traffic over 30 days and assume storage including indexes stays within 1 GiB.
At 100,000 reviewers: 30M reads, 15M writes, 800k deletes and 195.31 GiB outbound. Model Americas transfer at $0.12/GiB above 10 GiB.
Bursts, retries and retention can raise costs. Managed TTL, backups and point-in-time recovery are excluded.
¹ Choose one eligible host. Totals assume available free quotas and one Pro seat. Actual demo charges are unmeasured.
The head of customer success buys the workbench. A manager chooses where two interventions can make a difference this week.
Six fictional accounts expose conflicting signals, unresolved risks and missing evidence. Information requests use no slot.
The default queue sorts by attention group and then nearest renewal. The manager chooses the accounts and records the evidence.
Local work belongs to one browser profile. In Shared API mode everyone sees the same board. Each plan keeps its original evidence.
Measure the share of accounts renewing within 30 days with an evidence-linked plan, an owner and a follow-up by renewal.
The demo measures planning coverage. Evaluating renewal impact would require outcome data and a comparison group.
The static dashboard and Go service deploy separately. CI checks the frontend build and backend race tests and build.
The emulator supports shared-board checks, including competing writes, stale revisions and the reset cooldown.
PostHog records product events. Sentry reports errors from the browser and API.
The repository README links to local and shared walkthroughs, setup guides and the live API reference.
Public demo safeguards · controls and observable outcomes
The browser can read the fictional shared document. The API
validates every command. Local work stays in IndexedDB.
Two browser profiles in Shared API see the same committed plan.
Switch to Local to see only the current profile’s work.
The transaction reads the shared board, checks the account
revision and remaining capacity, then writes the updated board.
When two commands compete for the final slot, one commits.
The other receives a conflict. Editing a plan keeps its slot.
List, command and reset routes have separate in-memory quotas
per network peer and service instance. The board also records
a reset cooldown that survives restarts.
Throttled requests return 429 and Retry-After. Direct Firestore
subscriptions do not consume the API’s request quotas.
The API validates the command, account revision, time zone
and follow-up date. It caps command bodies at 8 KiB.
A stale revision returns a conflict. An invalid command leaves
the board unchanged. API errors carry a reason code.
A confirmed reset takes no request body. One transaction
clears edits and advances revisions for all six accounts.
An editor opened before a reset cannot overwrite the reset.
A second reset within 60 seconds returns a retry delay.
Resolve the issue → rule stops matching
Budget approval pending and renewal in ≤ 14 days
Adoption fell ≥ 30 points and sponsor is unreachable
30 matches; 29 does not; both parts required
No rule above matches and adoption or sentiment is unknown
Unknown is never read as 0% or as a fall
No attention rule matches and there is no active plan
No attention rule matches and an intervention is active
Resolving its issue keeps the slot occupied
A review-now signal remains after the intervention is completed
Completing the intervention frees its slot
Complete Ember’s plan, then save Beacon’s intervention.
Ember becomes Reviewed. Beacon takes the released slot.
Product and engineering trade-offs · delivered and at scale
Ember is seven days from renewal with budget pending. Cove has
a critical issue. The manager chooses which two plans to fund.
Give each team a planning period and its own capacity
Managers can inspect the signal behind each flag. Drift’s failed
report stays visible as missing evidence.
Compare thresholds with observed renewals and overrides
Open one account at a time
A focused detail panel keeps the evidence beside the action,
Add a comparison view if managers repeatedly switch
between detailed histories to choose an intervention.
IndexedDB stores the local board during an outage. Returning to
Shared API reconnects the listener. Local edits stay local.
If offline submissions are needed, queue intended shared
commands and resolve stale revisions and slot conflicts.
The API saves the plan and checks capacity in one transaction.
Browsers receive the committed board directly from Firestore.
If unrelated edits contend, split account documents and
keep capacity checks in the same transaction.
Anyone can try or reset the synthetic board. API request limits
apply per peer and instance. Reset also has a shared cooldown.
For customer data, scope access by workspace and role.
Use shared counters if quotas must span instances.
At scale · Workspace queue + detail panel
Proposed when several customer success teams manage private portfolios. Follow the same Cove and Drift cases through a team workspace.
Give Cove an owner and date.
Which account gets the team’s last slot?
The support incident gives Cove’s owner a concrete next step.
Drift’s missing report calls for investigation. A question uses
no slot. Each team has its own planning period and capacity.
Write the plan and slot together.
Save plans in this browser profile.
Local edits stay here on recovery.
another plan if the team is full.
